# Intake Brief — Visual representation of reputation (MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E)

Add an ambient, diegetic visual representation of the player's reputation to the Main Street street area: a population of small silhouette pedestrians ("stick people") whose number scales with reputation, who wander the street, and who dissolve into a stream of coins — flowing into the business coin grids — when the end-of-turn reputation income phase runs. This replaces the current reputation-phase animation in which coins fly from the HUD reputation counter into the businesses.

## Problem statement

Reputation is a core resource but has no persistent on-street presence: it surfaces only as a HUD number and the short-lived blue reputation pips in the HUD feedback. The street therefore does not communicate how reputable the player has become. This item makes reputation legible in the world — more reputation means a busier street — and gives the end-of-turn reputation income a diegetic source (the people themselves) instead of coins appearing from the HUD line.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — sees their standing in the town "come alive": a growing, wandering crowd that visibly turns into the reputation income flowing into their businesses.
- **Game designer / balancer** — gets a legible, glanceable scale for reputation, decoupled from the economy numbers.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the layer to remain presentation-only: deterministic, reduced-motion safe, replay/headless exempt, and non-blocking.

### User stories

- As a player, when my reputation grows the street fills with more pedestrians, so I can feel my progress without reading the HUD.
- As a player, at the end of the turn I see the pedestrians I have gathered dissolve into coins that flow into my businesses, so the reputation income has a visible, satisfying source.
- As a player with reduced motion enabled, I get no pedestrians or flights and the existing text/HUD feedback is unchanged.
- As a developer, the pedestrian population is derived from a pure function of reputation, so it is trivially testable and never couples to income/economy logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Producer polish pass 2 (during this session).** The producer refined the behaviour: figures walk on **one side of the road** (a lane offset), not the middle; shops are entered by **deliberate walking** (no teleport); the crowd **persists across street rebuilds** (a card played); and at the **end of the turn** non-shoppers walk **off the block** rather than vanishing, while enough figures walk into shops to source the income. Implemented by child `MS-0MUZ6CGSV002WTYM` (commit 3079ad7).

> **Producer polish pass 3 (during this session).** Pedestrians now always walk to the **nearest occupied cell**, and a cell filled mid-turn is picked up (retargeting every frame). In-shop figures spread to their own random interior spot. Implemented by child `MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2` (commit e3b67f7), building on `MS-0MUZ9CKT60094CXO` (cell spread) and `MS-0MUZ6CGSV002WTYM` (lanes/deliberate entry/persistence/walk-off).

> **Producer revision (2026-10-07).** A manual producer audit rejected the free-wander crowd. The pedestrians now walk the **roads only** and enter **occupied shops**; the crowd resets from the block corners each turn and the reputation income is sourced from the figures inside the shops (see AC2–AC4). Implemented by child `MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ` (commit 1c489ea).

1. **Pedestrian population reflects reputation.** A pure helper derives the figure count as `floor(reputation / 50)`, floored at 0 and **uncapped** (producer decision). Each figure is a small solid-colour silhouette in reputation blue (`#88bbff`), matching the existing reputation visual language. Verified by unit tests on the pure helper (0 rep → 0; 49 → 0; 50 → 1; 500 → 10; negative/NaN guarded).
2. **Pedestrians walk the roads.** Figures walk only on the road bands between and around the street cells (following the road network built from `mapRoadBands`), so a walking figure never crosses a business cell. Walking is presentation-only and does not consume gameplay RNG (a module-local seeded presentation PRNG isolated from the gameplay `state` RNG), so seeded determinism and headless/AI parity are preserved. Verified by a rendering behaviour/unit test asserting a walking figure's centre always lies on a road band, and by the existing determinism tests.
3. **Population updates live with reputation and resets each turn.** While a turn is in progress, a reputation gain fades a figure in and a loss fades a figure out, so the on-street count always matches the HUD reputation value. At the start of a new turn the crowd is cleared and a fresh set wanders onto the street from the four corners of the block. Verified by a unit/behaviour test driving a reputation change through the refresh path and a behaviour test asserting clear-then-respawn from the block corners.
4. **Reputation income is sourced from the pedestrians in the shops.** A figure may enter an **occupied** business cell (a player-owned `state.streetGrid` entry) to spend money and then stays there. In `animateIncomePhases`, the `'reputation'` phase no longer starts its coin flight at the HUD reputation counter (`{ x: gameW * 0.5, y: hudY }`); each business's coin stream dissolves out of a figure standing inside that business (falling back to any shop occupant, then a street-area anchor — **never** the HUD counter). By the start of the reputation income phase at least 25% of the live crowd is inside occupied cells (enforced deterministically, presentation-only). The credited coin count (`iconsForAmount(repBonus)`) is **unchanged** — the pedestrians are a visual source only, so the phase-sum invariant and the deferred-mutation economy are untouched. The `+total` landing pop and the phase pacing (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`) are unchanged. Verified by unit tests asserting the reputation phase's coin source/origin, the 25% occupancy minimum, and that the credited total is unchanged.
5. **Accessibility and non-rendering modes unchanged.** Reduced Motion skips the pedestrians and the dissolve-to-coins flights; replay/headless modes perform no rendering or audio. No new RNG consumption; determinism and headless/AI parity are preserved. The animation remains non-blocking — a throwing pedestrian layer must never stall the turn. Verified by unit tests for the reduced-motion/replay exemptions and by the existing determinism tests.
6. **Documentation updated.** `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` documents the new pedestrian layer, the live population rule, the reputation-phase conversion, and the reduced-motion/replay exemptions. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Build and full suite green.** New/updated unit tests pass, `npm run build` succeeds, and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only.** The pedestrian layer and the conversion must never mutate game state, the transcript, or the turn flow; every step is defensive and failures are swallowed so the turn always advances (matching the income-animation invariant, `ux-visual-audio.md`).
- **Do not change the economy.** The credited reputation income, phase-sum invariant, and deferred-mutation handling are untouched. Pedestrians are a visual source of the *existing* coin count, not a new producer.
- **Reduced motion + replay/headless exemption** are mandatory, following the established animator convention.
- **No new RNG consumption by gameplay.** Any randomness is presentation-local and must not draw from the seeded gameplay RNG.
- **Reuse existing VFX infrastructure.** Follow the primitive convention in the animator (`s.add.circle`, runtime-generated graphics textures); no new external art assets are required.
- **Do not shorten the phase pacing.** `INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` and the ≈11s collection landing are part of the presentation contract.
- **Minimal churn.** Touch only the street pedestrian layer and the reputation-phase animation path.

### Out of scope

- Changing any reputation/coin value or formula.
- Reputation visuals anywhere other than the street area (e.g. the challenge panel, scoreboard, or card art).
- Replacing the HUD reputation counter, the `+delta` HUD pop, or the Upcoming/incident reputation pip routing.
- Making pedestrians interactive (clickable, hoverable, gameplay-affecting).
- The tutorial's compact `animateIncomeCollection` choreography (unchanged).
- Per-seat competitive pedestrian populations (see the related-work note on `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I`; single human seat unless coordinated).

## Existing state

- `animateIncomePhases` (`src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`, `case 'reputation'`) animates the reputation phase: `from = { x: s.layout.gameW * 0.5, y: s.layout.hudY }` (the HUD reputation counter) and calls `flyCoinsIn(slot, amount, from, delayOffset, flightMs)` to fly each business's `repBonus` into its on-card coin grid via `revealInGrid`.
- The on-card coin grid (`src/coin-grid.ts`) uses `iconsForAmount(amount)` with `COINS_PER_ICON = 100`; the `+total` landing pop is produced by the collection phase.
- The income show order is `base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collect`, gated by `s.replayMode` and `s.settingsPanel?.reducedMotion` in every phase.
- The HUD reputation readout is rendered in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (reputation text, `repX`).
- The street area is described by `s.layout` (`streetTop`, `slotW/H`, `streetRowGap`, `streetCols`, `gameW`, `gameH`); `animator.getStreetSlotCenter(slotIndex)` gives slot centres; roads are drawn by `drawStreetRoads` using `roadBandThickness`.
- VFX in this codebase is generated from Phaser primitives (`s.add.circle`, `g.generateTexture(...)`), not pre-authored sprite sheets — there are no pedestrian/silhouette assets or code today.
- `MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8` ("Coin and Reputation should count up/down") is an open idea touching HUD reputation feedback; coordinate so the two do not conflict.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` ("Perform end of turn phase for each player") is at `intake_complete` and may extend the income presentation to per-seat competitive play; the pedestrian layer must not assume a single global reputation if that lands first.

## Desired change

- Add a new presentation module (e.g. `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts`) providing:
  - a **pure** `pedestrianCount(reputation)` helper (`floor(reputation / 50)`, min 0, uncapped);
  - a Phaser layer/manager that spawns the silhouettes in the street area, wanders them within bounds, and fades figures in/out as reputation changes;
  - a `dissolveIntoCoins(targets)` routine that turns the on-screen pedestrians into the coin stream used by the reputation phase.
- Add the layer to the scene lifecycle (create/update/resize/destroy) and refresh the population whenever the HUD reputation value changes.
- Change the `case 'reputation'` branch of `animateIncomePhases` to source its coins from the pedestrians instead of the HUD reputation line, keeping the credited amounts, `revealInGrid` landing, sfx, and pacing unchanged.
- Add named constants (ratio `50`, silhouette colour `0x88bbff`, size, wander speed, bounds padding).
- Update `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` and add unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — **new**: pure `pedestrianCount` helper, silhouette layer, wander animation, live population refresh, `dissolveIntoCoins`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `case 'reputation'`: source the coin flight from the pedestrians instead of `{ gameW * 0.5, hudY }`; keep amounts/landing/sfx/pacing identical.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` — expose the pedestrian layer/animator accessor (mirrors existing animator accessors).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — instantiate the pedestrian layer, drive its update, and refresh it on reputation changes; destroy on shutdown.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — hook the reputation-change path (or expose `repX`) so the population refresh triggers from the same place the HUD counter updates.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — new pedestrian constants (ratio, colour, size, speed, street bounds).
- `tests/main-street/` — new tests: pure count helper; live population refresh; reputation-phase source/origin; reduced-motion/replay exemption; credited-total invariance.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the layer, the conversion, and the accessibility exemptions.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8** (idea, open) — "Coin and Reputation should count up/down": a sibling change to HUD reputation feedback. Coordinate so the live pedestrian updates and the counter animation agree on timing.
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** (done, completed) — "Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback": the refactor the phased show sits on.
- **MS-0MUO7CPH3003TXFI** (done, completed) — "Reduce time upcoming event is shown": recent end-of-turn animation pacing work; the pacing contract this item must preserve.
- **MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I** (intake_complete, open) — "Perform end of turn phase for each player": may introduce per-seat income presentation; the pedestrian layer must not hard-code a single global reputation if this lands first.
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** (done, completed) — "Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD": relevant to how reputation is surfaced per seat.
- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** (core) — the phased income-grid animation epic that introduced the `base → … → collect` choreography and the `case 'reputation'` flight being replaced.
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** (plan_complete) / **MS-0MTSAWSME004BH6S** (done) — card-art work; this item uses Phaser primitives rather than new authored art, so it is independent, but shares the "visual richness of the street" theme.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: high-reputation crowding / performance.** The count is uncapped by producer decision, so a very high reputation could spawn many figures. Mitigation: use a single shared generated silhouette texture and lightweight tweens; keep per-figure work constant; measure at representative high reputation and document the result. Escalate to the producer only if frame cost is material.
- **Risk: presentation/economy coupling.** Mitigation: keep the count in a pure helper and assert in tests that the credited total and phase-sum invariant are unchanged.
- **Risk: determinism regression.** Mitigation: no gameplay-RNG draws; presentation randomness isolated (local seed or non-seeded tweens), with the existing determinism tests as the guard.
- **Risk: live-update storms.** Reputation can change several times per turn; a naive per-change rebuild could thrash. Mitigation: reconcile to the target count (add/remove the delta) rather than rebuild the layer.
- **Risk: competitive/per-seat conflict.** Mitigation: coordinate with `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I`; scope to the human seat and document the assumption.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Keep to the street pedestrians and the reputation phase; record any additional ideas (e.g. reputation-affected building facades) as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the population display is ambient and may appear in all play modes (including tutorial); only the *conversion* replaces the phased reputation phase, and the tutorial's compact collection is untouched.
- **Assumption:** pedestrians are non-interactive and have no gameplay effect.
- **Assumption:** the ratio, colour, silhouette style, and wander behaviour are as confirmed in the Appendix; the ratio (1 per 50) is a presentation constant, not a balance value.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (appearance, round 1): "What should the stick figures look like — (a) line-art, (b) solid-colour silhouettes, or (c) small detailed character sprites?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "1. B"** — small solid-colour silhouettes, no internal detail, in reputation blue (`#88bbff`). Source: interactive reply in this session. Research: existing reputation VFX uses the blue `0x88bbff` pip (`flyRepPips`, `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles`); VFX in the codebase is Phaser-primitive based (`s.add.circle`), so no authored art is required.
- Q2 (walking, round 1): "Where should they walk — (a) wander freely, (b) follow a fixed road loop, or (c) cluster around business slots?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "2. A"** — free wandering across the street area. Source: interactive reply. Research: the street area is bounded by `s.layout` and slot centres are available via `getStreetSlotCenter`; the road bands are drawn by `drawStreetRoads`.
- Q3 (ratio, round 1): "How many figures per reputation point — (a) 1 per 10, (b) 1 per 20, (c) 1 per 5, or (d) fixed count?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "3. b"** (1 per 20). **Revised (round 2, producer): "c but lets change the ratio to 1/50"** — final accepted ratio is **1 figure per 50 reputation, uncapped, minimum 0** (option c = uncapped 1:1 with `reputation / 50`). Source: interactive replies. Research: reputation is integer and card `reputationPerTurn` values are in the tens–hundreds (e.g. Clinic 160, Hotel 120), so 500 rep = 10 figures.
- Q4 (conversion semantics, round 2): "How should the figure→coin conversion read on screen, given the displayed figure ratio (1 per 50 rep) differs from the credited coin scale (`iconsForAmount`, 1 icon per 100 coins)?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "1. A"** — figures dissolve into a coin stream; each figure may spawn multiple coins, and the credited coin count is unchanged (presentation-only). Source: interactive reply. Research: the current `case 'reputation'` flies `flyCoinsIn(slot, amount, from = HUD rep line, ...)`; `amount = roundHalf(slot.pd.repBonus)` and the credited total is governed by the phase breakdown, so the visual can be re-sourced without touching the economy.
- Q5 (live vs end-of-turn population, round 2): "Should the figure count update live as reputation changes, or only at turn close?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "2. A"** — live fade in/out, matching the HUD reputation counter. Source: interactive reply. Research: `animateHudValueChanges` already observes coin/reputation deltas and is the natural refresh trigger; the HUD reputation counter is authoritative.
- Q6 (density cap, round 2): "How should extremes be handled — (a) min 0 / max 12, (b) min 1 / max 8, or (c) uncapped?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "3. c but lets change the ratio to 1/50"** — uncapped with the revised ratio. Source: interactive reply. Recorded as an accepted performance risk (see Risks & assumptions).
- Prior session (2026-09-19, `MS-C0MU7VAL20002XI99`): an earlier intake asked appearance/walking/ratio questions that were never answered. Those questions are superseded by the round-1/round-2 answers above; no duplicate work-item updates were made.



## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** – Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD (completed)
- **MS-0MUACDDMX004KWY8** – Bank your spare action is a dead end in the tutorial (open)
- **MS-0MUWE6OER004GNV1** – Full-suite verification and regression (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: animation, around, bonus, businesses, coins, create, current, end, fly, hud, line, move, replacing, reputation, small, sprites, street, them, there, they, turn, visual
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: animation, bonus, businesses, coins, create, current, end, fly, higher, hud, line, move, reputation, small, stick, street, them, they, turn, visual, walk
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: animation, bonus, coins, create, current, end, fly, hud, line, move, processing, reputation, small, sprites, stick, street, them, they, turn, visual

# Add test cases for AI and human win threshold in competitive mode

## Summary
Add test cases to `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-harness-smoke.test.ts` covering: (a) AI reaches threshold → human loss; (b) human reaches threshold → human win; (c) multi-AI scenario with human losing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — AI threshold win test:** A test using `buildHumanVsAis()` that sets an AI player's score ≥ `winThreshold` and asserts `gameResult === 'loss'` and `competitiveWinnerId === <ai_index>` when `checkCompetitiveEndConditions` is called.

2. **AC2 — Human threshold win test:** A test using `buildHumanVsAis()` that sets the human player's score ≥ `winThreshold` and asserts `gameResult === 'win'` and `competitiveWinnerId === <human_index>`.

3. **AC3 — Multi-AI threshold test:** A test with human + multiple AIs where the highest-scoring AI wins, asserting `gameResult === 'loss'` for the human and correct `competitiveWinnerId`.

4. **AC4 — All existing tests pass:** No regressions in the existing test suite.

## Implementation Notes

- Use existing test harness from `tests/main-street/helpers/competitive-fixtures.ts` (`buildHumanVsAis()`, `evaluateEndConditions()`).
- These tests must be added before the implementation fix so they initially fail, confirming the bug.
- The `findHumanSeatId()` helper exists and returns the human's index in `state.players` or -1.
- Key file: `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-harness-smoke.test.ts`

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-harness-smoke.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/helpers/competitive-fixtures.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` (reference for `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`)

# Intake Brief: Ownership-aware AI placement — do not place synergy that only benefits other players

**Work item:** MS-0MUYODDW300690KX · `bug` · `high`
**Discovered from:** observed competitive play — the AI places community spaces that anchor the human player's businesses but give the AI nothing
**Related precedent:** [MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW](MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW) (community-space scoring + business-preference penalty), [MS-0MT5X3N79002S038](MS-0MT5X3N79002S038) (competitive ownership-aware AI scoring)

## Headline

In shared-street (competitive) play the AI's placement scoring counts the synergy a card anchors for **every** neighbouring business, regardless of who owns it. A community space that only boosts an opponent's businesses can therefore score positive, and the AI spends coins and pays an ongoing running cost to enrich a rival. The competitive placement score must be ownership-aware: credit only the synergy the acting AI gains, and subtract (or refuse) the synergy it hands to other players, so the AI places a card only when **its own benefit exceeds the benefit it confers on others**.

## Problem statement

`scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` (used by both the single-player and competitive spend chains) computes a community space's value from `neighbourSynergyGain`, which sums the marginal synergy income added to **all** adjacent businesses with no owner filter. In single-player there is only the acting seat, so this is correct. In competitive/shared-street play (`state.ownerTaggedGrid` present, `isCompetitiveMode(state) === true`) the grid holds businesses owned by the acting AI **and** by other seats. When the AI considers a slot adjacent to an opponent's matching-synergy business — but not its own — `neighbourSynergyGain` still returns a positive number, so the community space can clear `COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY` and be bought/played. The AI then pays the placement cost and the `ongoingCost × horizon` drain to increase a rival's income.

The same blind spot applies to the other direction for any card: `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` measure only the placed card's own income + synergy and never account for the synergy the placement anchors for neighbouring **opponent** businesses. The seed's general rule — "only place cards (any cards) where the benefits to the AI are greater than to other players" — therefore is not met by the current competitive scoring.

Ownership is already modelled (`getSlotOwnerId` / `ownerTaggedGrid`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`) and used elsewhere in the competitive AI (`countOwnSynergyMatches`, `competitiveUpgradeTargets`), so this is a fix to the scoring path, not a new system.

## Users

- **Human player (seat 0) vs AI opponents** — a shared-street competitive game should not be handed an economic gift by an AI that anchors the human's businesses for free.
  - *"As the human player, I want the AI to compete for its own advantage, so my businesses don't get free synergy the AI paid for."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants competitive AI behaviour to follow the intended principle (own benefit ≥ benefit to others), with measurable before/after evidence and no change to single-player balance baselines.
  - *"As the producer, I want competitive AI placements to be ownership-aware so the AI plays to win rather than boosting opponents."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ownership-aware community-space value (competitive).** In competitive mode, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` (or a competitive variant invoked by `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore`) counts neighbour synergy only for slots owned by the acting player. Synergy anchored for a business owned by any other seat is not credited and is subtracted from the placement score, so the score reflects `own gain − opponent gain`.
2. **Opponent-only community space is rejected.** A community space placed into a slot whose only positive value is synergy for another seat's business scores `≤ 0`; `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` therefore returns `false` and the greedy AI does not buy or play it (measured by a unit test constructing an opponent-owned adjacent business).
3. **Self-beneficial placements preserved.** A community space whose synergy anchors the acting AI's own businesses retains a positive score and is still chosen; a community space anchoring a mix of own and opponent businesses scores strictly less than the identical placement with only own businesses (no regression for genuine self-interest).
4. **All competitive placements charge opponent benefit.** For ordinary business placements in competitive mode, the placement score subtracts the marginal synergy income the placement anchors for neighbouring **opponent** businesses (net differential), while the acting player's own income/synergy valuation is unchanged. The eligibility gate for income-producing businesses is unchanged (they remain always eligible); the differential is reflected in how they rank against alternatives.
5. **Single-player unchanged.** With no `ownerTaggedGrid` (N=1), `scoreAction`, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` and `GreedyStrategy` produce identical scores/decisions to today; `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` pass unmodified.
6. **Determinism preserved.** The same seed + same strategy yields an identical competitive action sequence (`CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`), and no RNG is introduced into the ownership-aware scoring.
7. **Evidence captured.** Before/after competitive head-to-head evidence shows the rate of placements conferring net benefit on opponents falls (net of single-player baselines, which are unchanged), committed alongside the change.
8. **Documentation updated.** The competitive placement rule (own benefit must exceed benefit handed to other seats) is documented in the AI strategy docs and code doc-comments, including the `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` / competitive-score comments.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Scoring heuristic only — no engine or rule changes.** Reuse the existing ownership model (`getSlotOwnerId`, `ownerTaggedGrid`) and the existing synergy computation (`computeSynergyBonus`); do not change income routing, `computeSynergyBonus` semantics, or the same-type penalty.
- **Single-player paths must remain behaviourally identical** (N=1 fallback), preserving the committed Monte Carlo balance baselines (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`).
- **Preserve the existing business-preference semantics** (`COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY`, positive-score eligibility for community spaces).
- **No new randomness;** scoring stays deterministic.
- **Reputation and shared/global effects** stay valued as they are today (reputation is per-owner; only synergy-attribution changes).
- **Scope-creep risk:** widening this into a full multi-seat minimax/opponent-modelling rework, or retuning card costs, is out of scope — record follow-ups as linked work items.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `neighbourSynergyGain(grid, placed, slotIndex, bonusPerNeighbor)` sums synergy gains for every neighbour with no owner filter (lines ~180–206). `communitySpacePlacementValueAt` uses it for `neighbourIncome`; `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` is the public entry point and is called from `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` (the "competitive mirror" explicitly documented in `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md`). `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` for ordinary businesses count only `(baseIncome + projectedSynergy) × horizon − cost`. `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gates community spaces on `score > 0`.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — `getSlotOwnerId(state, slotIndex)` (owner tag with active-player fallback) and `ownerTaggedGrid`; the established ownership source used by `countOwnSynergyMatches` and `competitiveUpgradeTargets`.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `computeSynergyBonus(grid, index, bonusPerNeighbor, soldSlots, gridDims)`; the ownership-agnostic per-card synergy used by the before/after diff.
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — competitive head-to-head harness (`runCompetitiveMonteCarlo`, `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`) for before/after evidence.
- Existing competitive scoring is already ownership-aware for events (`computeCompetitiveEventValue` counts only the acting player's matching businesses) and upgrades (own slots only); placement is the remaining ownership-blind path.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` (ownership-aware scoring, `place()` fixture tagging owners), `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` (single-player community-space value), `tests/main-street/no-phantom-synergy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/same-type-synergy.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce an ownership-aware neighbour-synergy attribution helper (e.g. `neighbourSynergyGainByOwner(...)` returning `{ own, opponent }`, or an optional owner filter on `neighbourSynergyGain`), using `getSlotOwnerId(state, i)` against the acting seat.
2. Use it in the competitive placement value so a community space's `neighbourIncome` credits only the acting player's slots and subtracts (or excludes and negatively weights) opponent slots, yielding an `own − opponent` net placement value.
3. Apply the same opponent-benefit term to the ordinary business competitive scores so any placement is penalised by the synergy it anchors for opponents.
4. Keep single-player `scoreAction` / `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` on the ownership-agnostic path (all slots belong to the acting seat) so baselines do not move.
5. Add focused unit tests (own-only, opponent-only, mixed) and capture before/after competitive Monte Carlo evidence; update the AI strategy docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — add ownership-aware neighbour-synergy attribution; thread it through `communitySpacePlacementValueAt` / `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` and `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore`; keep `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gating community spaces on the ownership-aware score.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — reference only (`getSlotOwnerId`, `ownerTaggedGrid`); no change expected.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — reference only (`computeSynergyBonus`); no change expected.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — new AC1–AC3 tests: opponent-owned adjacent business makes an opponent-only community space ineligible; own-only placement stays positive; mixed placement scores below own-only.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` — confirm single-player scores are unchanged (AC5).
- `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` — confirm `GreedyStrategy` decisions unchanged (AC5).
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — reference for the competitive harness; add/extend a report to capture opponent-benefit placement rate if needed.
- `src/scripts/balance/community-space-placement-report.ts` — reference/extension point for before/after evidence.
- `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the competitive ownership-aware placement rule (own benefit must exceed opponent benefit).
- `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md` — note that the competitive mirror is now ownership-aware.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW** (completed) — *AI uses community space cards too much.* Introduced `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement`, the neighbour-anchoring value and `COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY`; this item fixes the ownership blind spot left in that competitive mirror.
- **MS-0MT5X3N79002S038** (completed) — *Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free scoring for shared-street play.* Established the competitive scoring/enumeration layer this change extends; its AC1 ("ownership-aware scoring") currently covers resources/own businesses but not the synergy handed to opponents.
- **MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ** (completed) — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution.* Established per-owner income accrual on the shared street (why opponent synergy gain is a real benefit to a rival).
- **MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y** (completed) — *AI should not use Community Favour as much.* Same family of AI-heuristic corrections.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (from seed):** the target is competitive/shared-street play ("other players"); single-player has no opponent and must not change.
- **Assumption (from seed):** the general principle applies to *any* card, so ordinary business placements also subtract opponent benefit; the observed, most damaging case is community spaces.
- **Assumption:** "benefit to other players" from a placement means the marginal synergy income credited to their businesses; reputation/global events are out of scope (valued as today).
- **Balance risk:** subtracting opponent benefit could suppress legitimate business placements in tight shared-street configurations. Mitigation: keep own income/base value intact and subtract only the anchored opponent synergy; verify against the competitive harness that AI scores/win rate do not regress materially.
- **Baseline risk:** touching a shared helper could leak into single-player. Mitigation: explicit N=1 fallback and unchanged single-player tests (`community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts`, `ai-strategy.test.ts`, Monte Carlo baseline guardrail).
- **Determinism risk:** adding ownership lookups must not introduce ordering/RNG variance. Mitigation: AC6 determinism test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a full opponent-modelling/minimax rewrite, or cost retuning, is out of scope — record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope — which seats):** "Is this competitive (multi-seat shared-street) only, or also single-player?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "Competitive only. The seed says 'the player' and 'other players', and single-player has no opponent; `isCompetitiveMode` and `ownerTaggedGrid` already distinguish the two. Single-player behaviour must remain identical." Source: self-research of `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` (`isCompetitiveMode`, `getSlotOwnerId`) and `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md`. Accepted: competitive-only change with N=1 fallback.
- **Q2 (scope — card families):** "Which placements must be ownership-aware — community spaces only, or all cards?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "All cards, per the seed's 'any cards'. The scoring change is generalised, but community spaces are the observed defect and the primary acceptance test; ordinary businesses keep their own income and are penalised only by the opponent synergy they anchor." Source: seed description; `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` inspection. Accepted.
- **Q3 (objective function):** "Is the AI objective 'ignore opponent benefit' or 'maximise own benefit − opponent benefit'?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "'Own benefit − opponent benefit', per 'benefits to the AI are greater than to other players'. A placement that helps an opponent more than the AI should score ≤ 0 and be rejected for community spaces." Source: seed description; existing `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` `score > 0` gate. Accepted.
- **Q4 (verification):** "What proves the fix?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "Focused unit tests (own-only positive, opponent-only rejected, mixed scores below own-only) plus before/after competitive Monte Carlo evidence and the unchanged single-player suite/baselines." Source: `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` fixtures; `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`. Accepted.
- **No producer-blocking open questions.** The seed plus existing ownership infrastructure make the intent clear; assumptions above are recorded for producer confirmation at the review gate.

# Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge cards)

## Problem statement

Business and community-space cards are currently rendered with a neutral dark-grey
face (`#2f2f2f`); only a faint synergy-accent header bar, the 64×64 art backing and
the synergy icons carry the synergy colour. Players therefore cannot read a card's
synergy type — or, for a bridge card, both of its synergy types — directly from the
card face, which weakens at-a-glance planning when the market row mixes single- and
multi-synergy cards. The card face should be coloured by synergy type, and bridge
cards (exactly two synergy types) should show both colours, split top and bottom.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — scanning the market row and their street,
  wants to identify a card's synergy type(s) instantly without reading the icon row or
  opening a tooltip.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player scanning the market, I want each business/community-space
  card coloured by its synergy type, so that I can tell Food from Culture at a glance.
- As a Main Street player evaluating a bridge card, I want to see both of its synergy
  colours (top and bottom), so that I immediately understand it connects two clusters.
- As a player with colour-vision deficiency, I still want an unambiguous cue (the
  synergy icons), so that colour is not the only signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single-synergy face colour.** Every business and community-space card with
  exactly one synergy type renders its card face in that synergy type's face colour
  from a single shared, documented palette, replacing the current neutral `#2f2f2f`
  face. The mapping is the single source of truth used by every generator.
- **AC2 — Two-tone bridge face.** Every card with exactly two synergy types renders
  its face split horizontally into two colour bands — **top band = first entry in
  `synergyTypes`, bottom band = second entry** — using the same palette. The rounded
  card corners and the existing inner gradient / header-bar treatments are preserved,
  and neither band bleeds outside the rounded rectangle.
- **AC3 — Both synergies identifiable; colour is not the only cue.** Each bridge card
  continues to render **both** synergy icons (bottom-left), and the title/stat text
  remains white and legible on both bands; cards remain identifiable under hand
  overlap (~20 px) and street stacking (~23 px) (existing layout contract
  CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN). Cards with zero synergy types (event / upgrade / staff) keep
  their existing family colours unchanged.
- **AC4 — All render paths agree.** The static Node generator
  (`generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`), the runtime CSV fallback
  (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`) and the dynamic state-aware generator
  (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) all produce the same synergy colouring/split, and the
  pre-baked SVGs in `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` plus
  `csv-checksum.json` are regenerated.
- **AC5 — Tests.** Unit tests cover: single-synergy cards use the matching palette
  colour; bridge cards emit two bands with the correct top/bottom palette colours and
  band geometry; zero-synergy cards are unchanged; the TS and mjs generators agree;
  and the shipped static SVGs reflect the colouring (regression guard). Existing SVG
  tests (`card-svg-generator.test.ts`, `mjs-svg-generator.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`,
  currency/ongoing-cost tests) continue to pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, `README.md` where relevant, and the Main Street docs
  (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` bridge section and any card-rendering/design
  notes).
- **AC7 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Rendering-only:** no engine, rules, scoring, adjacency, balance, or card-data (CSV)
  changes. `synergyTypes` is already the source of truth.
- **One palette:** a single documented synergy→face-colour map is the source of truth.
  The `.mjs` static generator cannot import the TS module, so the values are duplicated
  in the two places with a test asserting agreement — following the existing pattern
  used for staff cost text.
- **Two types maximum today** (CSV distribution: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge,
  135 none). Behaviour for >2 synergy types is out of scope; the implementation must
  degrade safely (e.g. fall back to a single/first colour) rather than throw.
- **Preserve the existing card layout:** 64×64 left-art zone, text positions, cost
  badge, level badge, synergy icons and embedded art (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN).
- **UK English** in code comments and documentation.

## Existing state

- Runtime cards are rasterised from static SVGs generated by
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` (`generateCardSvg`) and refreshed
  from the CSV at runtime by `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts`), driven by `MainStreetSvgTextureManager`.
- `familyColor()` (mjs) and `cardColorScheme()` (TS) give business and community-space
  cards a neutral face (`#2f2f2f`); synergy colour is applied only to the graphic
  backing (`opacity 0.42`), the 20 px header bar (`opacity 0.18`) and the synergy icons.
- `synergyColor` (bright palette) is used for icons/accents; `CARD_BG` (dark palette)
  exists in the TS generator for `generateBusinessCardSvg` and is currently the only
  place a synergy-coloured face is used.
- 39 business/community-space cards: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge — Cafe, Food Truck,
  Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga Studio, Physiotherapist,
  Teahouse, Public Art.
- `generateBusinessCardSvg` (dynamic) is used only by tests today; the runtime texture
  path is the CSV/static pair — but it must stay consistent.

## Desired change

- Introduce a documented synergy→face-colour palette (reuse `CARD_BG`) and a helper
  that computes the face background: one colour for single-synergy cards, a top/bottom
  colour pair for bridge cards.
- Update the `.mjs` and TS generators to paint the face with that helper, splitting
  bridge faces horizontally (top = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom = `synergyTypes[1]`)
  inside the rounded rect (clip path or two rounded/clipped rects).
- Regenerate the static SVGs and `csv-checksum.json`.
- Add/update tests and documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — face background via palette +
  top/bottom split for bridge cards; expose the mapping for tests.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `cardColorScheme` /
  `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` and `generateBusinessCardSvg` face colouring + split;
  shared `CARD_BG` palette.
- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — canonical `synergyColor` (bright palette) reference;
  add the dark face palette here if it should be shared.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — regenerated, especially
  `biz-cafe.svg`, `biz-food-truck.svg`, `biz-gallery.svg`, `biz-spa.svg`,
  `biz-florist.svg`, `biz-juice-bar.svg`, `biz-yoga-studio.svg`, `biz-physio.svg`,
  `biz-teahouse.svg`, `cs-public-art.svg`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated checksum.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — read-only; verify the runtime CSV
  fallback picks up the colouring (no change expected).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — face-colour + bridge split
  assertions.
- `tests/main-street/mjs-svg-generator.test.ts` — static-SVG regression guard for the
  split + TS/mjs agreement.
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — verify no regression in art embedding with the
  new backgrounds.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — document the colour scheme / bridge two-tone rule.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN` (completed) — Synergy tooltip.
- `MS-0MTSAWSME004BH6S` (completed) — Add images for all cards.
- `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` (completed) — Competitive rendering: owner-coloured street,
  shared-market phase alternation, SFX.
- `MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327` (completed) — Move level label to left (same SVG layout code).
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` (open) — Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card
  (touches the art backing in the same generator).
- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` (open) — Identify different AI players (shared
  colour-blind-friendliness concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (palette):** use the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette for the card face
  (readable with white text), keeping the bright `synergyColor` palette for
  icons/accents. The producer may prefer the bright palette — a small, localised switch.
- **Assumption (split):** horizontal split, top band = first entry in the CSV
  `synergyTypes` order, bottom = second, matching the operator's "top and bottom".
- **Assumption (scope):** applies to business + community-space cards in all three
  generators; event/upgrade/staff keep family colours; no >2-synergy cards exist today.
- **Risk (generator drift):** the mjs and TS generators hold separate copies of the
  colour logic. Mitigation: shared constant values plus an agreement test.
- **Risk (contrast/readability):** full colour faces may reduce text contrast,
  especially under the 0.18 header overlay. Mitigation: dark palette, keep the synergy
  icons as a secondary cue, and visually check in the browser test.
- **Risk (stale static assets):** forgetting to regenerate the static SVGs / checksum
  leaves the game showing old faces. Mitigation: regenerate in the same change and add
  a shipped-SVG regression test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** card-art redesign, per-owner tile tints, or synergy-icon
  additions are out of scope — record as linked work items, do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive round was run — the operator's seed directive plus repo research
sufficed to draft a clear brief. The design defaults below are recorded as **assumed
(recommended option)**; the producer may override any of them before implementation.

- **Q1 (palette):** "Which palette should colour the card face?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette (Food `#5D4037`,
  Culture `#1565C0`, Commerce `#2E7D32`, Service `#6A1B9A`, Entertainment `#C62828`,
  Health `#00838F`), because white card text stays legible; the bright `synergyColor`
  palette stays for icons/accents. Source: repo research of
  `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.CARD_BG` and `MainStreetCardsUtils.synergyColor`.
  Status: **assumed**.
- **Q2 (split):** "How are a bridge card's two colours arranged?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): horizontal split, top band = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom band =
  `synergyTypes[1]`, matching the operator's wording "two colours top and bottom".
  Source: operator directive. Status: **assumed**.
- **Q3 (scope / render paths):** "Which cards and which generators?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): business + community-space cards in all three generators
  (static `.mjs`, runtime CSV TS, dynamic TS); event/upgrade/staff unchanged. Source:
  repo research. Status: **assumed**.

**Research summary (agent, 2026-10-08):** Verified via CSV that bridge cards are the 10
cards with two `synergyTypes` entries and that no card has more than two; located the
two runtime render paths (`MainStreetSvgTextureManager` → static SVGs +
`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`) and the test-only dynamic `generateBusinessCardSvg`;
confirmed the current face is neutral `#2f2f2f` with synergy only in the accent/header/
icons.

# Spread reputation pedestrians evenly around the street edges

## Problem statement

The reputation pedestrians (the on-street crowd that visually represents the
player's reputation) all enter the street from the four block corners and then
each walks to the **nearest** occupied business. Because the spawn points are
concentrated at the corners, the crowd clusters into whichever businesses sit
nearest those corners instead of being spread fairly evenly around the street,
so the visual representation of reputation looks lopsided.

## Users

- **Player (reputation visualisation):** sees the crowd as a stand-in for their
  reputation score; a lopsided crowd misrepresents the state and looks broken.
  - *As a player, I want the reputation crowd spread around the street so my
    reputation reads as a distributed, healthy population rather than a clot in
    one shop.*
- **Producer (manual audit):** rejected the corner-clustered distribution and
  wants figures to enter spread out around the four edges.
  - *As the producer, I want figures to enter spread out around the street so
    that when they head to the nearest business the crowd is naturally evenly
    distributed.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Perimeter spawn distribution.** New figures spawn at points distributed
   along all four edges of the road-network perimeter — including mid-edge
   positions — rather than only at the four block-corner nodes. A pure/behaviour
   test asserts that across a seeded run of `spawnPedestrianFigure` calls the
   spawn origins cover all four edges and that at least some figures originate
   away from corner nodes.
2. **Relatively even spread.** The spawn distribution is *relatively even*
   around the perimeter: over a seeded run the per-edge spawn counts fall within
   a defined tolerance of an equal share (roughly `N/4` per edge), and/or the
   perimeter positions are stratified so no region dominates. Deterministic with
   the presentation PRNG; a test asserts the per-edge balance.
3. **Road/lane invariants preserved.** Spawned figures still start on a road
   **lane** (offset from the centre-line, on a road band) and heading along a
   valid road segment (`from`/`target` endpoints of the perimeter segment).
   Existing lane/on-road assertions continue to pass.
4. **Nearest-business seeking unchanged.** Walking figures still head for the
   nearest occupied cell (MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2) and still walk deliberately into
   it with no teleporting; a behaviour test asserts that an evenly spread crowd
   entering shops distributes across more than one occupied business (rather
   than clustering in a single nearest shop).
5. **All spawn paths affected.** The even perimeter distribution applies to
   every spawn path — initial creation, `startNewTurn()` respawn, and live
   population reconciliation (`setPopulation` gains mid-turn) — not just the
   turn-start path. A test asserts reconciled/gained figures also spawn on the
   spread perimeter.
6. **Presentation-only behaviour preserved.** Reduced Motion and replay/headless
   exemptions are unchanged; no gameplay RNG is consumed; presentation-only
   failures are still swallowed; the credited reputation totals are unchanged.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` is updated to
   describe the even, edge-distributed spawn (replacing the "enter from a block
   corner / four corners" description), including unit test coverage for the
   distribution.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only layer: must never mutate game state, the transcript, or
  the turn flow; every public method stays defensive.
- Must use the module-local seeded presentation PRNG (`createPresentationRng`)
  and never the seeded gameplay RNG or `Math.random`.
- Must not change the figure count rule (`floor(reputation / 50)`) or the
  reputation-phase sourcing/25%-shopping guarantee.
- Keep the change surgical: no unrelated refactoring of the pedestrian layer.

## Existing state

- `spawnPedestrianFigure` (`src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts`) picks a random
  entry from `network.corners` and a random adjacent neighbour, then places the
  figure on the lane at that corner. All figures therefore originate at the four
  corners.
- `stepPedestrianFigure` re-resolves `nearestShop(figure, shops)` every frame
  and steers the figure toward the nearest occupied cell; if all figures start
  near the corners this concentrates them in the corner-nearest businesses.
- Docs (`docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`) currently state figures "always
  enter from a block corner" and "wander onto the street from the four corners
  of the block (`network.corners`)".
- Prior related work: `MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ` (road-walking / shop entry),
  `MS-0MUZ6CGSV002WTYM` (lanes, deliberate entry, persistence),
  `MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2` (nearest occupied cell seeking),
  `MS-0MUZ9CKT60094CXO` (in-shop spread).

## Desired change

Distribute spawn points (and thus entry points) evenly around the four edges of
the block perimeter rather than at the corner nodes only. Figures continue to
walk the road lanes and continue to seek the nearest occupied business, so an
evenly spread entry distribution yields an evenly spread crowd in the shops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — `spawnPedestrianFigure` and a new
  perimeter-distribution helper (stratified perimeter spawn points); keep
  `nearestShop` seeking intact.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — any new spawn-distribution constants.
- `src/MainStreetMapView.ts` — road-band/perimeter geometry helpers if needed.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — update the spawn/entry description.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-layer.test.ts` — spawn distribution tests.

## Risks

- **Distribution still imperfect when businesses are sparse.** If few cells are
  occupied, an even entry spread can still funnel several figures into the same
  nearest shop. Mitigation: scope is entry distribution only; shop seeking stays
  nearest-cell by design (producer phrasing).
- **Mid-turn spawns perturb the balance.** Live gains added between turns could
  bias one edge. Mitigation: apply the same stratified distribution on every
  spawn path; test reconciliation spawns.
- **Pure-helper coupling.** Changing spawn geometry could break existing
  lane/on-road invariants. Mitigation: keep the lane placement helper and assert
  the existing on-road/lane distance in the new tests.
- **Scope creep.** Related opportunities (retuning crowd density, per-seat
  competitive crowds, business-aware even assignment) are **out of scope** and
  should be raised as separate discovered-from work items, not absorbed here.

## Related work

See "Related work (automated report)" on the work item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** – Visual representation of reputation (parent epic)
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** – Competitive state model: per-player resources, owner-tagged street (completed)
- **MS-0MUVBH589001L7NL** – Competitive game ends on AI seat failure — reputation collapse or bankruptcy (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: around, block, business, corners, crowd (+12 more)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: around, block, business, cluster, edges (+11 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: block, business, corners, edges, enter (+10 more)


## Assumptions

- "Four edges" = the four sides of the road-network perimeter (the block
  boundary); the "street" is the road grid the figures already walk.
- "Relatively even" is enforced deterministically via a stratified/balanced
  distribution rather than left to chance, so it is testable.
- Shop targeting stays *nearest occupied cell* (per the producer's phrasing
  "when they go to the nearest business"); only the entry distribution changes.
- The even distribution applies to every spawn path, including mid-turn
  population gains.
- Buildings/roads/geometry are unchanged; this is a distribution change only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Interview skipped** — the seed intent from the producer was sufficiently
